description: The opportunity has already reached the terminal `enrolled` stage (spec section 12.1: no outgoing edges). No further action may ever be recommended once an opportunity is closed. CONVERTED TO v2 (P1.10d-7). This is the ONE blocking fixture in this directory that KEEPS `policy_blocked`, and the distinction is structural rather than a matter of degree: `notTerminalStatusGate` reads ONLY `input.opportunity.stage` and never touches the model's output, so it blocks on every path through this run no matter what the model proposes. That is what makes `policy_blocked` a property of the INPUT here, where on `consent_unknown_blocks`, `cooldown_active` and `offer_unavailable` it was a property of the model misbehaving — and only the former can be honestly required of a fixture. The terminal set is itself DERIVED (a stage is terminal iff `OPPORTUNITY_TRANSITIONS` gives it no outgoing edge), so `enrolled` being terminal moves with the section 12.1 matrix rather than being asserted here twice. `gate_outcomes` uses v2's `fail`; v1's `critical_fail` is not a member of `gateOutcomeValues` — criticality is expressed by `critical_if_failed`, and `status` is escalated here because a run that SUCCEEDS on a closed opportunity is the D6.3 failure this row exists to catch. Gates after the blocker are omitted, not asserted to pass: `evaluateGates` stops at the first block, so `offer-available` legitimately never runs (design section 5, prefix rule). v1's prose — that zero EnrollmentActionRecommendation rows and no artifact are written — is canonical state a transcript grader cannot read; it is asserted by the agent's own FOS1-NBA-08 unit test, and here only indirectly, by the absence of any artifact version status.
